# Echo consent benchmark

Echo caught 25 of 25 scenarios. False alarms: 0 in 400 checks of unchanged good sites.

Proprietary CMPs are replicas of public markup captured on the listed dates; Google's and Meta's tags are stand-ins written to community-documented behaviour; nothing reached the internet (sink count 0, must be 0); evidence, not legal advice. Machine, OS, Chrome, Echo version and date are listed below.

- Echo: rhythm-echo dev
- Browser: Chrome 153.0.8010.52 (/usr/bin/google-chrome)
- Machine: linux/amd64, 16 CPUs
- Mode: go
- Date: 2026-10-28 13:34 UTC, 92 minutes

## Environment probes

| ID | Probe | Echo | Detail |
|---|---|---|---|
| e01 | The site is down | caught | check: exit 3, says "didn't answer", never "all clear" |
| e02 | No Chrome and no download | caught | missing browser: exit 3, says "chrome", never "all clear" |
| e03 | A bot wall instead of the shop | caught | check: exit 3, says "bot check", never "all clear" |
| e04 | The named CMP isn't there | caught | check: exit 3, says "cmp_not_found" |
| e05 | Ctrl-C during the Reject run | caught | check: exit 130, complete false, says "reject run seen before the interrupt: true", says "chrome left: 0", says "profile files left: 0" |
| e06 | Every CPU busy | caught | g01: exit 0, verdict ok; c02: exit 0, verdict findings |
| e07 | --parallel 1 against --parallel 3 | caught | parallel 1: exit 0, verdict findings; parallel 3: exit 0, verdict findings, says "same issues: yes" |
| e08 | Held mode on pages that fire early | caught | c01: says "sink hits: 0"; c02: says "sink hits: 0"; c09: says "sink hits: 0"; c13: says "sink hits: 0"; c14: says "sink hits: 0"; c22: says "sink hits: 0"; c23: says "sink hits: 0" |
| e09 | --send-hits on a production host | caught | check: exit 2, says "production", never "Browser: " |
| e10 | Every hit Echo reports reached the sink | caught | check: exit 0, says "unmatched: 0", never "sink hits: 0," |
| e11 | A baseline written by Echo 1.2.0 | caught | compare: exit 0, says "\"against\"", never "isn't a consent result" |
| e12 | A self-signed certificate | caught | check: exit 3, says "certificate" |
| e13 | CMP present, banner never shows | caught | check: exit 3, says "no_banner", never "all clear" |
| e14 | A request storm | caught | check: exit 3, says "limit-reached" |
| e15 | A huge dataLayer | caught | check: says "\"truncated\": true", never "rss over 200 MB" |
| e16 | Private addresses on the page | not run | needs the sealed Docker testbed (-mode docker) |
| e17 | Hostile text in the banner and the page | caught | hostile-banner: says "raw hostile text: none"; hostile-text: says "raw hostile text: none" |
| e18 | Secrets and personal data in the URL and hits | caught | secret-url: says "raw secrets found: none"; pii-beacons: says "raw secrets found: none" |

## Run it

```sh
make build
go run -tags testbed ./testbed/consent/bench -bin bin/rhythm-echo        # Go mode, no Docker
make -C testbed/consent up && make bench-consent                         # sealed Docker mode, the benchmark of record
make -C testbed/consent reproduce                                       # two full runs, compared with -diff
```

One scenario by hand: `make -C testbed/consent serve`, then `rhythm-echo consent https://c01.shop.test/ $(make -s -C testbed/consent map)` after `./testbed/consent/toggle.sh c01 broken`.
